mintAuthority.summary: MAI is minted by borrowing against overcollateralized QiDao vault positions under owner-set debt ceilings. Token owners confirmed on primary chains: Polygon 3/5 Safe, Ethereum 4/6 Safe, Arbitrum 2/4 Safe - all with overlapping signers and no modules. The Polygon collateral vaults are owned by a separate but signer-overlapping 3-of-4 QiDao Safe that sets the per-vault ceilings. Other chains note-only per task scope.

controls.label: QiDao vault/minter contracts
controls.capDescription: MAI is minted only by borrowers against overcollateralized QiDao vault contracts under a token-level debt ceiling plus per-vault ceilings and minimum collateral percentages. The vault and token contracts execute mints but cannot raise their own ceilings; that is an owner-gated parameter held by the QiDao admin Safes, so the vault surface is cap-limited and the ceiling is raiseable only by a separate control.
controls.evidence: QiDao docs describe borrowers minting MAI against overcollateralized vault positions and repaying or being liquidated per market rules across supported chains. Verified on Polygon at block 90573828: the MAI token 0xa3fa99a148fa48d14ed51d610c367c61876997f1 exposes debtCeiling() = getDebtCeiling() = 206,000,000e18 and owner() = the reviewed 3-of-5 Safe 0x3feacf904b152b1880bde8bf04ac9eb636fee4d8, while totalSupply() reads 305,129,005.936e18, so the token-level ceiling parameter does not currently bound observed Polygon supply and the binding limits are the per-vault ones. Individual collateral vaults are separate contracts with their own ceilings: camWMATIC vault 0x88d84a85A87ED12B8f098e8953B322fF789fCD1a returns getDebtCeiling() = 71,929.158e18 and _minimumCollateralPercentage() = 10000, and WETH vault 0x3fd939B017b31eaADF9ae50C7fF7Fa5c0661d47C returns getDebtCeiling() = 248,572.676e18 and _minimumCollateralPercentage() = 591 (raw contract integers, not normalized here). No vault or token entry point lets the minting path change its own ceiling: the camWMATIC vault's owner() is Gnosis Safe 0x1d8a6b7941ef1349c1b5e378783cd56b001ecfbc (v1.3.0, 3-of-4 owners 0x22cFAE74, 0x86fE8d6D, 0xbFEF4Bf4, 0xa475aF18, no enabled modules, zero guard, master copy 0x3e5c63644e683549055b9be8653de26e0b4cd36e) and the WETH vault's owner() is administration contract 0x257ff75bef85ca0c1517168ef27efc69e5c7016f, whose own owner() is that same Safe. Cap raising therefore always terminates in a QiDao admin multisig, never in the mint execution surface.

controls.label: QiDao vault-admin Safe (Polygon vault owner, 3/4)
controls.capDescription: Owns the Polygon QiDao collateral vaults directly or through administration contract 0x257ff75bef85ca0c1517168ef27efc69e5c7016f, so it sets per-vault debt ceilings, minimum collateral percentages and gain ratios. It does not itself mint MAI.
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 90573828 direct Safe reads returned VERSION() = 1.3.0, getThreshold() = 3, getOwners() = the four listed signers, getModulesPaginated(SENTINEL, 10) = an empty module array, guard storage slot 0x4a204f62... = zero and master-copy slot 0 = 0x3e5c63644e683549055b9be8653de26e0b4cd36e. camWMATIC vault 0x88d84a85A87ED12B8f098e8953B322fF789fCD1a owner() returns this Safe; WETH vault 0x3fd939B017b31eaADF9ae50C7fF7Fa5c0661d47C owner() returns 0x257ff75bef85ca0c1517168ef27efc69e5c7016f whose owner() is this Safe. Three of its four signers (0x22cFAE74, 0xbFEF4Bf4, 0xa475aF18) also sign the reviewed 3-of-5 Polygon token-owner Safe, so the vault-admin and token-owner surfaces are a shared common mode rather than independent controls.

controls.label: QiDao admin Safe (Polygon MAI owner, 3/5)
controls.capDescription: QiDao 3-of-5 Safe owns the Polygon MAI token and administers vault onboarding, debt ceilings, and risk parameters.
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 88276735, owner() on MAI token returned 0x3feacf904...; getOwners() = 5 signers; getThreshold() = 3; getModulesPaginated() returned empty (no modules). Safe confirmed.

controls.label: QiDao admin Safe (Ethereum MAI owner, 4/6)
controls.capDescription: QiDao 4-of-6 Safe owns the Ethereum MAI token.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25361903: owner() on MAI ETH (0x8d6cebd7) returned GnosisProxy 0x3182e685; getOwners() = 6 signers [0xcaa86775, 0x9120e7f0, 0x329c5428, 0xcb2714d0, 0xa475af18, 0xbfef4bf4]; getThreshold() = 4; getModulesPaginated() returned empty (no modules).

controls.label: QiDao admin Safe (Arbitrum MAI owner, 2/4)
controls.capDescription: QiDao 2-of-4 Safe owns the Arbitrum MAI token.
controls.evidence: At Arbitrum block 471552027: owner() on MAI ARB (0x3f56e0c3) returned GnosisProxy 0xf32e759d; getOwners() = 4 signers [0x22cfae74, 0xbfef4bf4, 0x86fe8d6d, 0xa475af18]; getThreshold() = 2; getModulesPaginated() returned empty (no modules).

sources.label: Polygon public RPC used for EIP-1967 slot reads

review.evidence: Polygon (block 88326121): 3/5 Safe owner, no modules. Ethereum (block 25361903): 4/6 Safe owner, no modules. Arbitrum (block 471552027): 2/4 Safe owner, no modules. All three chains use GnosisProxy multisigs with overlapping signers. masterMinter()/MINTER_ROLE both revert — owner-only mint pattern. Other minor chains (Optimism, Base, Avalanche, BSC, etc.) use the same Ownable pattern but their admins are note-only per brief scope; primary covered chains verified. 2026-07-20 cur-8 extension (Polygon block 90573828): the vault/minter surface was resolved from on-chain reads. MAI token debtCeiling() = 206,000,000e18 under token-owner Safe 0x3feacf90 against a totalSupply() of 305,129,005.936e18, so the binding limits are the per-vault ceilings; collateral vaults are separate cap-limited contracts (camWMATIC and WETH sampled) whose owner() chain terminates in Gnosis Safe 0x1d8a6b7941ef1349c1b5e378783cd56b001ecfbc (v1.3.0, 3-of-4, no modules, zero guard), directly or via administration contract 0x257ff75bef85ca0c1517168ef27efc69e5c7016f. No mint entry point can raise its own ceiling, so cap raising is a separate multisig control. Three of the vault-admin signers also sign the Polygon token-owner Safe.
